definitions.gloss: to pile up; to stack up
definitions.explanation: to place things on top of each other to create a stack
to gradually gather or develop over time through sustained effort

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}がブロックを{積|つ}み{上|あ}げている。
examples.english: The child is stacking up blocks.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{経験|けいけん}を{積|つ}み{上|あ}げてきた。
examples.english: I have accumulated years of experience.

examples.japanese: {信頼|しんらい}は{一日|いちにち}で{積|つ}み{上|あ}げられない。
examples.english: Trust cannot be built in a day.

examples.japanese: レンガを{丁寧|ていねい}に{積|つ}み{上|あ}げる。
examples.english: I carefully stack up the bricks.

examples.japanese: {努力|どりょく}を{積|つ}み{上|あ}げてきた{結果|けっか}だ。
examples.english: This is the result of accumulated effort.

notes:
{積|つ}み{上|あ}げる is a compound verb meaning to pile up or accumulate.

VERB TYPE:
- Ichidan verb (る-verb)
- Transitive
- Intransitive pair: {積|つ}み{上|あ}がる

ETYMOLOGY:
- {積|つ}む (to pile, stack) + {上|あ}げる (to raise)

SENSE 1 VS SENSE 2:
- Sense 1: Physical stacking (boxes, blocks, bricks)
- Sense 2: Abstract accumulation (experience, trust, achievements)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {経験|けいけん}を{積|つ}み{上|あ}げる (to accumulate experience)
- {実績|じっせき}を{積|つ}み{上|あ}げる (to build up achievements)
- {信頼|しんらい}を{積|つ}み{上|あ}げる (to build trust)
- {荷物|にもつ}を{積|つ}み{上|あ}げる (to stack luggage)
- {努力|どりょく}を{積|つ}み{上|あ}げる (to accumulate effort)

INTRANSITIVE PAIR:
- {積|つ}み{上|あ}がる: Something piles up on its own
- {積|つ}み{上|あ}げる: Someone actively piles something

RELATED WORDS:
- {積|つ}む (to pile - base verb)
- {蓄積|ちくせき}する (to accumulate - more formal)
- {重|かさ}ねる (to layer, repeat)

REGISTER: Neutral. Common in everyday speech and business contexts.
